correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the frozen RESULT.md rather than from the saved audit. For the non-regular integral path complex, the allowed 2-paths split by endpoints exactly as claimed: each \(c_i\to c_{i+2}\) class has the two routes through \(c_{i+1}\) and the appropriate pole, giving the boundary \(R_i\), while each pole-to-itself class contributes differences of same-parity spoke cycles. No other missing-shortcut class permits cancellation. The underlying directed graph has cycle-lattice rank \(4n-1\); the \(4n\) cycles \(R_i,T_i\) have the single primitive alternating relation. Quotienting by the \(R_i\) boundaries and the same-parity \(T\)-differences leaves two generators \(U,V\) with relation \(n(U-V)=0\), hence \(\widetilde H_1(D_n;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) for every \(n\ge2\).
